title: Boyle's law: squeezing a gas
goal: See how the pressure of a fixed mass of gas changes when its volume changes at constant temperature.
note: Air in a syringe has a pressure and a volume. Pushing the piston in makes the volume smaller and the pressure larger, while pressure times volume stays the same.

graphs.title: The pressure falls as the volume rises.
graphs.label: Gas pressure

sentences: The air in the syringe starts at 108 kPa when its volume is 60, and its temperature stays the same.
A fixed mass of gas at constant temperature has a pressure that is inversely proportional to its volume.

predict.prompt: A syringe of trapped air is pushed in, so the air takes up less volume, at the same temperature. What happens to the pressure of the air?
predict.reveal: Move the volume below its starting value and watch the pressure.

concept_check.question: At constant temperature, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is made larger. What happens to its pressure?
concept_check.explanation: For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume, so a larger volume means a smaller pressure.

hints: Keep the temperature and the amount of gas the same.
What happens to the pressure when the gas is squeezed into a smaller volume?
Pressure times volume stays the same for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature.
